chronic_conditions: History of Graves' disease treated with radioactive iodine ablation

encounters.cc: Routine follow-up for hypothyroidism with two months of increasing fatigue, dry skin, and cold intolerance despite medication adherence.

lines: Routine follow-up for hypothyroidism with two months of increasing fatigue, dry skin, and cold intolerance despite medication adherence.
She reports feeling increasingly fatigued over the past two months, despite adhering to her usual medication regimen and sleep schedule.
She also notes that her skin has become drier and she often feels cold, even in warm environments.
She has not experienced any changes in weight.
Three months ago, she was started on oral estrogen therapy for menopausal symptoms.
- History of Graves' disease treated with radioactive iodine ablation
She has a history of hypothyroidism and has been stable on levothyroxine for several years.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative assistant.
Her physical examination is unremarkable except for mild bradycardia.
- Serum Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH): 7.2 mIU/L (reference range: 0.4-4.0 mIU/L)

encounters.cc: Three-month history of right shoulder pain worsened by overhead reaching activities at work.

lines: Three-month history of right shoulder pain worsened by overhead reaching activities at work.

This 47-year-old female with hypothyroidism following radioactive iodine ablation for Graves' disease, last seen in Endocrinology two months prior for fatigue and cold intolerance, presents with a 3-month history of right shoulder pain.
She reports that the pain worsens when she reaches overhead to file documents on high shelves, which is a frequent part of her job.
She denies any trauma or injury to the shoulder.
- History of Graves' disease treated with radioactive iodine ablation
Her medical history is significant for hypothyroidism.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative assistant.
On physical examination, there is tenderness to palpation over the lateral aspect of the right shoulder.
Pain is elicited during the Neer and Hawkins tests.
Passive range of motion is full, but active abduction is painful between 60 and 120 degrees.
There is no erythema, warmth, or swelling.
An X-ray of the shoulder shows no bony abnormalities.

encounters.cc: Persistent facial rashes for several months that worsen with sun exposure.

lines: Persistent facial rashes for several months that worsen with sun exposure.
This patient with Graves' disease and hypothyroidism, seen in Endocrinology, presents with facial rashes.
She reports that these rashes have been present for several months and seem to worsen with sun exposure.
She denies any joint pains, oral ulcers, or systemic symptoms.
- Shoulder impingement syndrome of right shoulder (diagnosed 2020-03-15)
- History of Graves' disease treated with radioactive iodine ablation
Her medical history is significant for hypothyroidism.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative assistant.
On physical examination, you note well-demarcated, erythematous plaques with central hypopigmentation and peripheral hyperpigmentation on her cheeks and nose.
Some of the plaques have a scaly surface, and there is evidence of atrophy and scarring.
No other skin lesions are noted elsewhere on her body.
She has no lymphadenopathy, and the rest of the examination is unremarkable.
A skin biopsy of one of the lesions is performed, and histopathology shows interface dermatitis with a perivascular and periadnexal mononuclear infiltrate.

encounters.cc: Six-month history of intensely pruritic skin lesions beginning on wrists and spreading to trunk and ankles.

lines: Six-month history of intensely pruritic skin lesions beginning on wrists and spreading to trunk and ankles.
This patient with hypothyroidism returns to dermatology following prior care for facial rashes.
She reports that the lesions started on her wrists and have since spread to her trunk and ankles.
She denies any new soaps, lotions, or medications.
- Shoulder impingement syndrome of right shoulder (diagnosed 2020-03-15)
- History of Graves' disease treated with radioactive iodine ablation
Her medical history is significant for hypothyroidism,.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative assistant.
On physical examination, you note multiple flat-topped, purple, polygonal papules on her extremities and trunk.
Some of the papules have fine white lines on their surface.
Oral examination reveals white reticular patches on the buccal mucosa.
A skin biopsy of one of the lesions is performed and shows hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and a band-like infiltrate of lymphocytes at the dermoepidermal junction.

encounters.cc: Six-month history of morning joint stiffness lasting over one hour, bilateral hand and wrist swelling, and unintentional weight loss.

lines: Six-month history of morning joint stiffness lasting over one hour, bilateral hand and wrist swelling, and unintentional weight loss.
The patient is a 48-year-old female with hypothyroidism and Dermatology evaluation for discoid lupus and lichen planus, who presents with new joint complaints.
She reports that her symptoms are most severe in the morning, lasting for more than an hour before improving with activity.
She also notes bilateral swelling in her hands and wrists.
She has experienced intermittent low-grade fevers and a 5-pound unintentional weight loss over the past few months.
- Shoulder impingement syndrome of right shoulder (diagnosed 2020-03-15)
- History of Graves' disease treated with radioactive iodine ablation
Her medical history is significant for hypothyroidism.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative assistant.
On physical examination, there is soft tissue swelling and tenderness over the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints bilaterally.
There is no evidence of joint deformity.
Radiographs of the hands show periarticular osteopenia and marginal erosions.

encounters.cc: Six months of fatigue and persistent nocturnal pruritus unresponsive to antihistamines with two months of progressive jaundice.

lines: Six months of fatigue and persistent nocturnal pruritus unresponsive to antihistamines with two months of progressive jaundice.

The patient is a 49-year-old female with Graves' disease status post radioactive iodine ablation, hypothyroidism, discoid lupus, lichen planus, and rheumatoid arthritis who presents with a 6-month history of fatigue and persistent itching.
She reports that the itching is worse at night and does not improve with over-the-counter antihistamines.
She also notes that her skin has become progressively yellow over the past two months.
- Shoulder impingement syndrome of right shoulder (diagnosed 2020-03-15)
- History of Graves' disease treated with radioactive iodine ablation
Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism, for which she takes levothyroxine.
She has no history of alcohol abuse and denies any recent travel or high-risk sexual behaviors.
On physical examination, she is afebrile with normal vital signs
Her skin and sclerae are icteric.
Abdominal examination reveals hepatomegaly without splenomegaly or ascites.

encounters.cc: Referred for four months of progressive fatigue, cold intolerance, six-kilogram weight gain, constipation, and irregular scant menses.

lines: Referred for four months of progressive fatigue, cold intolerance, six-kilogram weight gain, constipation, and irregular scant menses.

The patient is a 50-year-old female with a history of Graves' disease treated with radioactive iodine ablation and hypothyroidism on levothyroxine, previously evaluated in 2020 for fatigue and cold intolerance, who is referred for evaluation of progressive fatigue, cold intolerance, and a 6-kg weight gain over the past 4 months.
She also reports new-onset constipation, muscle cramps, and a feeling of "sluggish thinking" at work.
Her menses have become scant and irregular.
- Shoulder impingement syndrome of right shoulder (diagnosed 2020-03-15)
- History of Graves' disease treated with radioactive iodine ablation
Blood pressure of 110/70 mm Hg, heart rate of 58/min
Reflexes reveal delayed relaxation of the ankle jerk.
The thyroid gland is not palpable or tender on examination.
Visual field testing in the office demonstrates bitemporal peripheral vision loss.
A basic metabolic panel is normal except for mild hyponatremia.
The clinician orders thyroid function tests.

encounters.cc: Progressive vision difficulties causing clumsiness, worsening pressure-like headaches, and amenorrhea for one year.

lines: Progressive vision difficulties causing clumsiness, worsening pressure-like headaches, and amenorrhea for one year.
Patient returns for evaluation with a history of Graves' disease treated with radioactive iodine, chronic hypothyroidism, and previously diagnosed central hypothyroidism.
She says, "I keep stumbling into furniture and door frames." She also reports dull, pressure-like headaches that have worsened over the past few months.
Her last menstrual period was about one year ago; prior to that, her menses were regular every 25–30 days and lasted 3–4 days.
- Shoulder impingement syndrome of right shoulder (diagnosed 2020-03-15)
- History of Graves' disease treated with radioactive iodine ablation
Her medical history includes hyperthyroidism, treated with radioactive iodine 10 years ago.
Her father died of colon cancer at age 65.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative assistant.
She denies hot flashes or night sweats.
On examination, her blood pressure is 130/78 mm Hg, heart rate is 72/min, and BMI is 29 kg/m².
On breast exam, bilateral milky discharge is noticed upon palpation of the areola.
Brain MRI reveals a 2.5 cm suprasellar mass compressing adjacent structures.
